title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
interviewAnswer: CDC captures inserts, updates and deletes from source systems so downstream stores can update incrementally without repeated full extracts. Log-based CDC is common for low-latency replication.
why: Change Data Capture (CDC) is a recurring foundation across data science and machine learning because it affects both theoretical correctness and practical system behavior.
deepDive: CDC captures inserts, updates and deletes from source systems so downstream stores can update incrementally without repeated full extracts. Log-based CDC is common for low-latency replication. Deletes/tombstones need explicit handling. Exactly-once downstream effects require idempotency/transactions. The interview-level skill is not merely recalling the definition: explain the assumptions, what diagnostic evidence you would inspect, and what alternative you would choose when those assumptions fail.
workedExample: Stream database order changes into a warehouse/lake rather than reloading the entire orders table nightly.
commonMistakes: Using the concept mechanically without checking assumptions or data semantics.
Reporting one metric/result without examining uncertainty, slices or failure modes.
followUps: What assumptions or limitations does Change Data Capture (CDC) have?
How would you validate Change Data Capture (CDC) on a real dataset?
production: In production, make assumptions explicit, validate on representative slices, compare with a simple baseline and monitor the signals that can drift.
